game.context: after Sicario; free with ads on YouTube
game.hot_take: saw it coming the whole time. in the world of Black Mirror it didn't slap as hard as it probably did in 1997

moon.hot_take: omg i finally watched MOON! i enjoyed that very much. keeps the brain moving and had some stunning visuals. always kinda waiting for a BIG twist but it just happens slowly over time which is also really fun. what a performance. i could use a moon2 to do some more explaining but for the most part and for a 90min movie, it was largely successful i think!!!

stby.context: Free on Tubi. Slot two of the Tue Jul 21 double feature, after Nightcrawler 4.6. Top guess: multiverse (Coherence/EEAAO antibodies attacking the wrong disease — he was clocking Boots Riley magical realism as dimensional bleed). Genre-defection thesis landed: you cannot out-think a movie willing to breach its own genre contract. Took the dehumanization deal twice in one night (Nightcrawler, then WorryFree) — clocked and owned it. 4.8 ties Enemy on the podium step below BR2049.
stby.hot_take: "YOURE FUCKING KIDDING" — audibly yelled at the empty apartment when the horse cock flopped. Went in armed ("i think i gotta fuckin know"), spent the whole movie trying to outsmart the swerve because I said he never would, lost anyway. Declared a long-digest marinater, then twenty minutes later: "4.8 full send."

tdkr.context: Sunday solo rewatch. Completes the Nolan Batman trilogy in three days (Begins + Dark Knight Jul 24, Rises Jul 26). Long-gap rewatch: he had forgotten the Talia reveal entirely. FIRST HAZY WING EXIT - seen but unrateable before tonight, now carries a live score.
tdkr.hot_take: On whether Rises flipped his pro-Ra's verdict from the Begins debrief: "yeahhhh it pretty much did. Nolan knows his way around a story arc for damn sure. loved it. i had even forgetten the final twist!! haha god bless a bad jmemory it was fun all over again" Then: "oooooof okay i think this one goes 9.6"

cmiyc.hot_take: a classic. yearly christmas movie energy, home alone vibes at points. very clever very fun. didn't hit as hard but the enjoyment and pleasure watching was immense.

enemy.hot_take: what. the. fuck. — NO CLUE what that was, A TARANTULA?! Then cracked it himself in debrief: one man, and Adam is the alibi. "He invented the innocent. cute shy history teacher he dreams of being instead of the monster he sees himself as. ugh so good."

ncfom.hot_take: SPLIT WATCH ASTERISK (Jul 18 night one, Jul 19 finish) — his verdict: splitting it was the mistake, momentum broke. First-watch read: "i don't really get what all that was about... didn't really do much for me" — then rated it 4.1 anyway once the wrong-protagonist/elegy architecture clicked. Craft respected, meal denied by design. Also: "the bad guy with the fucking cunt ass bob." Flagged for a far-future one-sitting rewatch.

se7en.context: solo, bracket night two, first watch with the box unspoiled
se7en.hot_take: yes a really brilliant plot and WHATS IN THE BOXXXXX is so iconic i love love. brad pitt is incredible in this. that whole scene was just a masterclass.

batman.context: Second film of Jul 24, after The Nice Guys. Bought the Dark Knight trilogy by accident and started it instead of any of the four epics pitched (Apocalypse Now, Princess Mononoke, Beau Is Afraid, Suspiria). Long-gap rewatch; said most of it felt new. Sided with Ra's al Ghul on the burn-it-down argument. Praised the fear toxin portrayal as fully holding up. What felt new was the how and why, the mechanics; his memory had compressed it to cave, mountain, becomes batman.
batman.hot_take: ive seen all of these batman movies but not for a long time! lots of this felt new again. i loved it. so well told, and a fabulous story. but the cynic in me is pretty much like yeah, he's right, starting over is a historically accurate thing that happens so like maybe lets try that

br2049.hot_take: him finding out he was not special was truly heartbreaking… the way he kills Luv is fun as fuck

matrix.hot_take: HOWWWW have i never seen that movie before?! Screamed out loud at "dodge this."

amadeus.hot_take: the dictation scene was absolutely everything. salieri: so sad. so lame. THE LAUGH, grew to absolutely love it.

memento.context: Streamed on Peacock. Antibodies did not save him — structure can't be spoiled. Insulin question left unresolved on purpose.
memento.hot_take: MY GOD WHAT THE FUCKKKKK BRO ... this has been my favorite thus far. it deserves the 5.0 and everything else should be lowered a percentage

sicario.hot_take: amazing. big effort big pay off. love love. [Amended Jul 25, 2026: raised 9.8 to 9.9. "sicario beats those. bump sicario to 9.9 it needs it's own number for sure"]

maverick.context: Streamed on Paramount+. Picked as rough-day counterprogramming after Memento — did its job, craft praised, melodrama docked.
maverick.hot_take: i liked it! it was entertaining. i guess it mostly did it's job haha but the storyline and dramatics were just a bit over the top in all the places for a better rating haha but the action and awesome fucking planes and plan was good!

niceguys.context: Daytime day-off pick, rented (~$4), watched mid-music-editing afternoon. Picked over The Fifth Element, Hunt for the Wilderpeople, and Train to Busan (ruled out for subtitles). Called it "a fun lil flick." Found Holly a little annoying by the end but understood her role; agreed the funniest material is failure comedy, not banter.
niceguys.hot_take: yeah Gosling and the physical comedy was the best part by a long shot. overall, 8.6

oblivion.context: Saturday Aug 15 space/spy/high-tech slate, lead pick, included on Prime
oblivion.hot_take: OOOO and then immediately oh yeah that makes sense. Maverick with drones.

pressure.hot_take: Pretty decent! Mostly a weather report after all, but a good historical drama.

stardust.hot_take: just lovely!! another classic for the evening. the fucking score was just stunning throughout. de niro served all night. fabulous movie. 9.0 solid

sunshine.hot_take: "Fun little thing." Spent a big chunk going stacked cast, well made, why haven't I heard more about this... "then all of a sudden i was like oh. that's why hahahaha." Speedran the 2007 reception history in real time. Verdict on the third act: Door B (turn-as-thesis) is "reaching a bit too hard for an idea that didn't land" — read Pinbacker's god complex straight off the screen, no commentary track required.

triangle.context: Midday solo watch, pitched same day for WTF craving
triangle.hot_take: Sally pile and the birds were the two "ahh shit she's never getting out of this" hits. Loop done well.

barbarian.context: wine night, early night, guessed from the clue "doors doors doors"
barbarian.hot_take: "jesus christ i have so many feelings about that fucking goddamn mothershitting movie." Better than Sunshine, just under Pressure. The Justin Long smash cut fully conned him — thought the movie was OVER. Docked for the stairs problem (nobody should descend) and wanting one more layer on the Frank flashback. Proposed the tactically correct survival strategy: baby-voice "please mommy" total surrender. Collateral damage: The Ronettes, ruined in general.

coherence.context: Streamed on Prime/Peacock. Ending theory: we did NOT end with the same Em.
coherence.hot_take: it wasn't just 2 houses. or 3. its fucking infinite bitch

exmachina.context: double feature after Blade Runner 2049; free with ads on YouTube

gladiator.context: solo, Sunday, Paramount+. Lead of the Sep 13 epic slate (seven cards, all epic lane, after he rejected the first three). His own Sep 9 narrow finally watched.
gladiator.hot_take: ugh so many good moments but finally getting to hear and see the context of ARE YOU NOT ENTERTAINED was iconic.

malignant.context: Slot two of a Sunday double feature (after The Dark Knight Rises). Picked off a bizarre-and-fucked slate he asked for. NEW FLOOR: first film to score below The Game (6.8). Produced a permanent twist-calibration rule.
malignant.hot_take: Opening reaction: "andddddd yikes. voldemort did it first and was way more chill about it haha" Then the diagnosis: "nahhhh it didn't really work for me. it kinda hands you the probablity of it being her the whole time fairly early on and then by the time we get to ole voldy on the back it's not the reveal i wanted it to be. but the killing got way cooler after that haha"

obsession.hot_take: Group watch with John and Tori. "Fun watch... i think it was more john and tori's speed. overall entertaining just not real deep or truly satisfying." Clocked the One Wish Willow premise as tidy but shallow — high-functioning machine, modest reach.

rogue-one.hot_take: Really good and fun. "A star wars movie without jedis....? what are we even doing here?" — then immediately conceded the thesis: hallway scene certified absolutely badass, lands BECAUSE nobody has magic to answer it. First-ever Star Wars entry point, watched as the accidental perfect prologue. Unlocked the whole bracket: A New Hope next, Sith holds his purge question, Andor waiting.

spotlight.context: solo, Sunday, YouTube free. Back half of a double after Gladiator (9.7). His own queue, pitched as lead of the true-story slate, ranked "closest", then chosen over The Report and Margin Call.
spotlight.hot_take: spotlight was soooo good. what a fucking story man.

the-sting.context: solo, free on YouTube w/ ads. Benched twice before finally happening. Left a voice memo at minus-35 predicting a hidden con under the con, Luther alive, and Lonnegan in on it. Zero for three, delighted anyway. Identified Robert Redford via Barbra Streisand's husband and Jeremy Jordan.
the-sting.hot_take: oooo i loved it so much!!!! i had 6 million ideas about what was happening and it really was just simply happening in front of me. the audience just doesn't see the full extent and magnitude of the con! so fun! and snyder getting FUCKED in the middle of it was just awesome. i KNEW the FBI place was a fucking build as well but just was under the wrong assumption haha

darkknight.context: Third film of Jul 24. TRIPLE FEATURE FRIDAY: The Nice Guys, Batman Begins, The Dark Knight. Started 9pm. Long-gap rewatch. Sent in with a homework lens: track what the Joker says versus what he does. His Harvey read: the burn did not make him, he used it as permission to act on what he already wanted. His Joker read: the not-a-schemer speech means he has a plan but forty-five backups, and the planning and games are the fun. Produced a life principle he asked to save permanently (see journal_entries, category principle, Jul 25): self worth is not attached to any single plan landing.
darkknight.hot_take: good fucking god that's a great movie!!! the joker is really something else. i think dark night is a solid 9.8

hereditary.context: Friday Aug 14 spectacle/shock slate, the free-on-Tubi backup pick over Uncut Gems
hereditary.hot_take: WHAT THE FUCK MAN. Anxiety is not excitement, and I am not doing the homework.

inside-man.context: solo, weekend bracket night one, self-picked from the guessing-night slate
inside-man.hot_take: okay so he basically just built a shitty apartment in the ground in a bank and lived there for a week to steal some diamonds and out a nazi?

poorthings.context: Rental, weird night Thu Jul 23, his gut pick held against Titane / Sacred Deer / Annihilation challengers. Debrief: clocked the Oz black-and-white-to-color grammar himself; read Bella as fascinating, "enviable and a lesson of what not to do at the same time" (refined together to PRE-social, not antisocial: the anti-Leonard, zero self-deception, rules only kept if they survive her testing); Duncan arc hate-to-pity on schedule (shame economy bankruptcy); goat man sentenced gleefully. First film scored NATIVELY in the ten-point era. 9.3: alone on her own step, above Coherence, one tenth under Nightcrawler/StBY.
poorthings.hot_take: Raw reaction in three acts: "my first question is why. closely followed by what. then immediately becoming the fuck." Then: "why was it willy wonka wicked and wizard of oz fucking themed?!" On the ending: "FUCK the goat man. bye bye enjoy the grass forever."

silverlake.context: Solo watch, free on Roku Channel. Picked over The Handmaiden to avoid subtitles.
silverlake.hot_take: I have no fucking clue. Haha my gut says he's def the dog killer and maybe also the owl killer and this is his whole delusion to keep from recognizing that. Is he searching for god?

baby-driver.context: Saturday Aug 15 nightcap, third film of the triple-feature weekend, Leonard hard-called it solo
baby-driver.hot_take: The genius is in the verbs, not the nouns. Big fan.

bullettrain.hot_take: love lemon and tangerine!!!! the tank engine shit was good. brad pitt was incredible. might watch Thomas episodes tonight.

frost-nixon.context: solo, Friday, his rental. Picked off the Sep 10 re-pitch slate (Valkyrie was Leonard's lead; he took the talky one).
frost-nixon.hot_take: enjoyed very muich. very clever. very smart. very intense. good watch overall!

in-the-grey.context: solo, weeknight, his own Prime rental. Set out for Valkyrie, got "bamboozled" by Gyllenhaal on the way. Not a Leonard pick. Reopened the fun lane himself. "I would recommend this to a certain type of people without shame."
in-the-grey.hot_take: it was alright. daddies jake and henry were really the whole point. fun shooting and fighting and escaping etc but the script and plot felt very rough draft. entertaining and daddylicious but honestly the main character was the worst actress of them all and realy made you wonder why anyone was trying to save her hahaha

source-code.context: Fresh pitch same night, day 2 of dwdPS Season 1. The Moon bloodline pick.
source-code.hot_take: oooo this is a great movie / oh nooo so cheeeesy / love saves the day blah blah / then lame ending / then actual ending that is actually back ti pretty trippy and fun and woahhhhhh

the-amateur.hot_take: solid movie. mostly enjoyed. very smart stuff which was fun although the tech seemed highly unrelalistic haha

annihilation.context: solo watch, wiped after 6 hours of rehearsal
annihilation.hot_take: for me it was mostly the script that was just not there for me. visuals were lovely and the storyline was pretty entertaining and it was a fun watch, but nothing really mattered or the emotions weren't high enough. i didn't realy care about any of them and then they were dead haha and idk. we saw the lena with the tattoo get blown up but then why were her eyes shimmering at the end? did i miss something or just poorly explained or fucvking what?

nightcrawler.context: Free w/ ads on Tubi. 5pm curtain, earliest start of the ritual era — slot one of the promised Tuesday double feature. Debrief theories, all his: suspected Lou was orchestrating the crimes for a large chunk (pre-crime — act three makes him right), found the only lie in the film instantly (the story to the detective), read Nina as targeted-from-day-one due diligence, and nailed the single-emotion count in one guess (the mirror smash). 4.6 ties Coherence on the board.
nightcrawler.hot_take: okkkkkkkk i really enjoyed that!! kinda in love with lou hahaha — then scored it "9.6!" (Olympics judging incident, corrected: 4.6)

the-departed.context: Divorce papers signed earlier that day. Asked for mind-blowing Oscar-tier. Solo watch, rental.
the-departed.hot_take: woah woah woah wow wow holy fuck ... rat on rat on rat on rat and not believing anybody on not believing anybody. and just bullshit after bullshit. jesus christ, a fucking phenomenal movie

the-big-short.context: solo weeknight, pitched and watched same night, Paramount+
the-big-short.hot_take: yessss! so so similar to one battle after another in so many ways. so quirky and fun and cute and informative which really invites you to be open and learn new complicated things but not think too much about them. then holy fuck it opens up a whole crisis scenario play out over years that feel like real time. then it gets SOOOO SATISFYING and then not two seconds later it's like holy siht well fuck these people we have been loving from the get go are actually also just fucking idiot monsters who didn't realize if they bet against the ECONOMY there would be NO ECONOMY left to pay them out!!!!! like fucking idiots!!!!

disclosure-day.context: Friday afternoon double feature, slot 1. Amazon rental. NEW BOARD FLOOR, dethroning Malignant 5.4.
disclosure-day.hot_take: holy fucking shit that was a terrible fucking movie hahaha ... it was all speech for like the last hour. then we finally get the big alien "reveal" but we have been seeing what they look like for 45 min. so this was just the biggest alien??? and like why? and who? and the house building? for fucking why? and then the animals?! i was too stunned by the stupidity i ddin't even notice hte john williams. which means he probably saw what a dumb fucking script it was too and phoned it in haha 5.2 for this bitch

predestination.context: dwd Season 1 opening night; emotional day, wanted a full brain takeover
predestination.hot_take: he her them are also the baby that is her he him

la-confidential.context: Solo, Mon Aug 31. Picked off the Oscar slate, the 138-minute one, over the weeknight ceiling on purpose.
la-confidential.hot_take: good movie!! jesus christ how ANY crimes got solved before fingerprints is just a goddamn miracle haha

minority-report.context: Thursday solo pick. Beat Leonard's guessing game with the "saxophonus interruptus" clue (the sax kid in the jetpack tenement raid). Leonard guessed Jurassic Park, then cited the wrong sax scene. Double fault, flawless victory Dixon. Sparked the resonance-not-craft rating doctrine.
minority-report.hot_take: I liked that. That was a big, huge movie. I think overall just way too long. the whole pre cog thing just really never landed. And, like, the weird pre come, dizzy milk thing that they have to sit in... then she, like, turns into eleven from stranger things, and they go on a little adventure, and she's fine. And then, really, they're just crack kids. But then the final reveal of the guy, like, using the system against itself and doing the murder in the same way. Like, that all came together really nicely, and maybe that's why it had to be six hours long is to get us to that point.

operation-finale.context: Mon 9pm solo, picked off slate three after two whiffed slates and a Munich detour
operation-finale.hot_take: OOOOOOF the fucking house was nuts. brutal and insane. loved it. we always knew that's who he was and it was nice to finally get it in full force. isaac all the way

inglourious-basterds.context: Solo Monday night. Third slate of the session after two historical/science slates whiffed and Incendies was declined (no dead mom). Historical ask answered in his real lane.
inglourious-basterds.hot_take: those god damn NAAAAZZZIIIIISSS. such a fun movie. such wonderfully interwoven plots. BURN THAT FUCKER. landa was insane!!! also kinda iconic and giving queen behavior. brad pitt was incredible, his opening speech is kinda FIERCE. (on learning it was all invented:) fun to know it was all fuckin bullshit hahaha

one-battle-after-another.context: solo Tuesday night, first watch. Pitched as the crack-the-9s slate lead, chosen over Michael Clayton. Rental, broke the weeknight runtime ceiling happily.
one-battle-after-another.hot_take: what a MOVIE! such a fun ride. soooo many iconic things ... ooooof this is a big one. it realy got me gurl. 9.8 full send

masters-of-the-universe-2026.hot_take: oh my god. That movie was so fucking fun. I loved every minute of it. I think Skeletor is my new favorite villain of all time.
